edges.description: Most tested alleles form no functional gap junction channels on their own.
Several alleles do not reach the plasma membrane and accumulate inside the cell.
edges.target: Mutant Connexin 50 Mistrafficking and Intracellular Retention

edges.description: Some alleles inhibit or alter channels formed with co-expressed wild-type Cx50 or Cx46.
edges.target: Dominant Inhibition of Wild-type Lens Connexins

edges.description: The G46V allele traffics normally but produces abnormally large hemichannel currents.
Protein that never reaches the membrane cannot form intercellular channels.
edges.source: Mutant Connexin 50 Mistrafficking and Intracellular Retention
edges.target: Reduced Lens Fiber Gap Junctional Coupling

edges.description: ER-retained mutant connexin activates the unfolded protein response.
edges.source: Mutant Connexin 50 Mistrafficking and Intracellular Retention

edges.description: Fewer conducting Cx50 channels lower coupling between fiber cells.
edges.target: Reduced Lens Fiber Gap Junctional Coupling

edges.description: Loss of Cx50 delays organelle and nuclear degradation in maturing fibers.
Cx50-mediated communication is needed for the postnatal peak of lens epithelial mitosis.
edges.target: Impaired Postnatal Lens Epithelial Cell Proliferation

edges.description: Retained organelles in central fibers are a plausible source of light scatter; the cited studies show the defect alongside the cataract but do not show that it causes the opacity.
Inhibition of wild-type channels lowers fiber cell coupling below the level set by the mutant allele alone.
edges.source: Dominant Inhibition of Wild-type Lens Connexins
edges.target: Reduced Lens Fiber Gap Junctional Coupling

edges.description: Excess hemichannel opening increases apoptosis of expressing cells.
Proposed by the authors as a cytotoxic route to opacity; not demonstrated in a lens.
Reduced outflow of water and ions through fiber gap junctions disturbs the lens circulation.
edges.source: Reduced Lens Fiber Gap Junctional Coupling

edges.description: Calcium builds up in central fibers until it precipitates.
The precipitates form where the opacity forms.
Fewer epithelial divisions give a smaller lens.
edges.source: Impaired Postnatal Lens Epithelial Cell Proliferation

edges.description: Small lens and eye growth produces microphthalmia.
Microcornea accompanies the cataract in many human families; that it arises from the same growth defect is an inference from the mouse data, not a demonstrated link.
Null mice have microphthalmia, small lenses and zonular pulverulent nuclear cataracts.
edges.limitations: Complete loss of Cx50 models recessive null alleles; most human disease is heterozygous missense, which may also inhibit wild-type connexins.

edges.description: Null lenses lack the postnatal mitotic peak of the lens epithelium.
edges.limitations: Not examined in human GJA8 lenses.
edges.target: Impaired Postnatal Lens Epithelial Cell Proliferation

edges.description: Heterozygous and homozygous lenses have reduced Cx50 and Cx46 levels and reduced fiber coupling.
edges.limitations: Mouse missense allele; the human change at the same residue, D47N, behaves differently in vitro (it forms heteromeric channels with wild-type connexins).
edges.target: Reduced Lens Fiber Gap Junctional Coupling

edges.description: Calcium precipitates in homozygous lenses match the distribution of the cataract.
edges.limitations: Precipitates were shown in homozygotes; human dominant disease is heterozygous.

edges.description: The G22R allele is loss of function for Cx50 and reduces phosphorylated Cx46 in vivo.
edges.limitations: The same G22R substitution was later found in BALB/c dense cataract and microphthalmia (dcm) mice with recessive inheritance (PMID:20861565), so its dominance in mice is not fixed.
edges.target: Dominant Inhibition of Wild-type Lens Connexins

edges.description: Heterozygotes have pulverulent cataract with smaller eyes; homozygotes have marked microphthalmia with a hypoplastic lens.
edges.limitations: Rat N-terminal missense allele not reported in humans.

nodes.description: Lens extraction for visually significant opacity, followed by optical correction (contact lens or intraocular lens) and amblyopia therapy. The cited outcomes come from infantile cataract cohorts of all causes. Visual axis opacification and glaucoma are the main long-term complications. No GJA8-specific therapy exists.

evidence.reference_title: Current management of infantile cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Better visual outcomes in operated eyes, however, are achieved in the setting of early presentation, bilateral infantile cataracts, absence of nystagmus or strabismus, and consistent amblyopia therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Current management of infantile cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The most common complications of cataract surgery performed in infancy are visual axis opacification and, in about a third of patients, the long-term development of glaucoma.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical interventions for bilateral congenital cataract in children aged two years and under.
evidence.snippet: There is no high level evidence for the effectiveness of one type of surgery for bilateral congenital cataracts over another, or whether surgery itself is better than primary aphakia.

nodes.description: Bilateral lens opacity present at birth or in early childhood; the defining feature of the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic heterogeneity in microcornea-cataract: five novel mutations in CRYAA, CRYGD, and GJA8.
evidence.snippet: One mutation (P189L) affected the gap junction protein alpha 8 (GJA8), and one mutation (Y134X) was detected in crystallin gamma-D (CRYGD).

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in GJA8 associated with autosomal dominant congenital cataract and microcornea.
evidence.snippet: GJA8 mutations were seen in two of the 60 unrelated probands with cataracts.

nodes.description: First extracellular domain; severe microphthalmia and sclerocornea in a de novo case, and acorea-microphthalmia-cataract in a Japanese family.

evidence.reference_title: Association of variants in GJA8 with familial acorea-microphthalmia-cataract syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, another variant, NM_005267.5:c.151G>A (p.D51N) in GJA8, was identified to co-segregate with this syndrome in an unrelated Japanese family.

nodes.description: The avascular lens depends on an internal circulation of ions and water that leaves the fibers through gap junctions. When connexin coupling falls, intracellular hydrostatic pressure and free calcium rise in the fibers.

evidence.reference_title: The Connexin50D47A Mutant Causes Cataracts by Calcium Precipitation.
evidence.snippet: Cx50D47A expression altered the lens internal circulation by decreasing connexin levels and gap junctional coupling.

evidence.reference_title: Connexin Mutants Compromise the Lens Circulation and Cause Cataracts through Biomineralization.
evidence.snippet: The expression of the dominant mutants causes severe decreases in connexin levels, reducing the gap junctional communication between lens fiber cells and compromising the lens circulation.

nodes.description: Mutant subunits co-assemble with wild-type Cx50 or Cx46. P88S and P88Q abolish or reduce wild-type Cx50 coupling, V44E silences channels formed with wild-type Cx46 and Cx50, and S50P and D47N form heteromeric channels with altered properties. This is one way a heterozygous variant can cause disease while null alleles are recessive in mice.
nodes.id: Dominant Inhibition of Wild-type Lens Connexins

animal_models.description: The G22R allele is loss of function for Cx50 and reduces phosphorylated Cx46 in vivo.
animal_models.name: Gja8 G22R (Lop10) mouse

evidence.reference_title: Functional effects of Cx50 mutations associated with congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: However, the mutant did not form functional gap junctions when expressed alone, or with wild-type (WT) Cx46 and Cx50, indicating that V44E is a dominant negative inhibitor of WT connexin function.

evidence.reference_title: The cataract-inducing S50P mutation in Cx50 dominantly alters the channel gating of wild-type lens connexins.
evidence.snippet: However, the mixed expression of Cx50-S50P and wild-type subunits of either Cx50 or Cx46 - to create heteromeric gap junctions - resulted in functional intercellular channels with altered voltage-gating properties compared with homotypic wild-type channels.

evidence.reference_title: A Gja8 (Cx50) point mutation causes an alteration of alpha 3 connexin (Cx46) in semi-dominant cataracts of Lop10 mice.
evidence.snippet: Targeted null mutations in Gja8 and Gja3 in mice cause cataracts with recessive inheritance.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of Gja8 (alpha8 connexin) in mice leads to microphthalmia associated with retardation of lens growth and lens fiber maturation.
evidence.snippet: while the alpha8 heterozygous (+/-) mice have relatively normal eyes and lenses.

nodes.description: First extracellular domain; zonular nuclear pulverulent cataract.

evidence.reference_title: Connexin 50 mutation in a family with congenital "zonular nuclear" pulverulent cataract of Pakistani origin.
evidence.snippet: Here we describe a second mutation (E48K) in connexin 50 that confirms the involvement of this gene in cataractogenesis.

nodes.description: The G46V allele, found in a child with congenital total cataract, forms functional gap junction channels but hemichannels with much larger currents than wild type; its expression kills cells, and high extracellular calcium prevents the death. This route has been shown only in cultured cells and oocytes and only for this allele.

evidence.reference_title: A mutant connexin50 with enhanced hemichannel function leads to cell death.
evidence.snippet: The biochemical results indirectly suggest a potential novel mechanism by which connexin mutants could lead to cataracts: cytotoxicity due to enhanced hemichannel function.

nodes.description: First extracellular domain; congenital total cataract. Traffics normally but forms hyperactive hemichannels that kill expressing cells.

evidence.reference_title: A mutant connexin50 with enhanced hemichannel function leads to cell death.
evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing of the GJA8 gene identified a 137 G>T transition that resulted in the replacement of glycine by valine at position 46 of the coding region of CX50 (CX50G46V).

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in the human connexin50 gene (GJA8) underlies autosomal dominant "zonular pulverulent" cataract, on chromosome 1q.
evidence.snippet: These studies provide the first direct evidence that GJA8 plays a vital role in the maintenance of human lens transparency and identify the genetic defect believed to underlie the first inherited disease to be linked to a human autosome.

nodes.description: Germline GJA8 variants alter connexin 50. Most are heterozygous missense substitutions, many in the first extracellular and transmembrane domains (P88S, P88Q, E48K, V44E, W45S, G46V, D47N, D51N, V79L); the recessive alleles are frameshifts that replace the C-terminal part of the protein. Different alleles act through different routes: absent channel function, failure to reach the plasma membrane, dominant inhibition of wild-type lens connexins, altered gating, or, for G46V, excess hemichannel activity.

evidence.reference_title: Functional effects of Cx50 mutations associated with congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Thus, each mutation produced distinct changes in the properties of junctional coupling.

nodes.description: Earlier proposed as a cataract allele; found in an unaffected parent and forms normal channels, so it is treated as a rare polymorphism.

evidence.reference_title: The GJA8 allele encoding CX50I247M is a rare polymorphism, not a cataract-causing mutation.
evidence.snippet: Although the CX50I247M substitution has previously been suggested to cause cataracts, our genetic, cellular, and electrophysiological data suggest that this allele more likely represents a rare silent, polymorphic variant.

nodes.description: Maturing lens fibers normally degrade their nuclei and organelles. In Gja8 null and Cx50 D47A mouse lenses, nuclear remnants and organelle proteins persist in deep fibers and some crystallins are reduced. Whether this contributes to the human opacity has not been tested.

evidence.reference_title: Connexin50D47A decreases levels of fiber cell connexins and impairs lens fiber cell differentiation.
evidence.snippet: They also implicate Cx50 in fiber cell differentiation, since mutant lenses showed impaired degradation of organelles and decreased levels of some crystallins.

evidence.reference_title: Connexin50D47A decreases levels of fiber cell connexins and impairs lens fiber cell differentiation.
evidence.snippet: The lenses of Cx50D47A mice showed persistence of nuclear remnants in deep regions of the lens

nodes.description: Without Cx50, lens epithelial cells do not reach the normal mitotic peak of the first postnatal days, so lenses contain fewer cells. Knock-in of Cx46 in place of Cx50 only partly rescues this, so the requirement is specific to Cx50.
nodes.id: Impaired Postnatal Lens Epithelial Cell Proliferation

animal_models.description: Null lenses lack the postnatal mitotic peak of the lens epithelium.
animal_models.name: Gja8 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Connexin50 is essential for normal postnatal lens cell proliferation.
evidence.snippet: On P2 to P3, wild-type lenses displayed a significantly increased MI not evident in knockout lenses, and knockin lenses only partially rescued the growth deficit.

nodes.description: Pulverulent opacities in a lamella surrounding the nucleus.

evidence.reference_title: A novel GJA8 mutation is associated with autosomal dominant lamellar pulverulent cataract: further evidence for gap junction dysfunction in human cataract.
evidence.snippet: The pulverulent cataract described in this family is associated with a novel GJA8 mutation and has a different clinical phenotype from previously described GJA8 mutants.

nodes.description: Insoluble calcium precipitates form in Cx50 mutant mouse lenses with the same distribution as the opacity, suggesting that the cataract results from biomineralization within the lens. Shown in mice; not examined in human GJA8 lenses.

animal_models.description: Calcium precipitates in homozygous lenses match the distribution of the cataract.
animal_models.name: Gja8 D47A (No2) mouse

evidence.reference_title: The Connexin50D47A Mutant Causes Cataracts by Calcium Precipitation.
evidence.snippet: Alizarin red-stained calcium precipitates were present in homozygous Cx50D47A lenses with a similar distribution to the cataracts.

nodes.description: Death of cells expressing the hyperactive G46V hemichannel. Shown in HeLa cells, not yet in lens tissue.

evidence.reference_title: A mutant connexin50 with enhanced hemichannel function leads to cell death.
evidence.snippet: CX50G46V-induced cell death was prevented by high concentrations of extracellular calcium ions.

nodes.description: Lenses of Cx50 S50P and G22R mice show raised BiP and increased Xbp1 splicing. The authors judge the response too modest to be a major driver of the cataract, so this node is a contributing branch rather than the main path, and no edge from it to the opacity is asserted.

evidence.reference_title: The unfolded protein response is activated in connexin 50 mutant mouse lenses.
evidence.snippet: Overall, these data suggest that UPR may be a contributing factor to the phenotype of connexin 50 mutant lenses even though the relatively modest extent of the response suggests that it is unlikely to be a major driver of the pathology.

nodes.description: Homomeric channels of most cataract-associated Cx50 mutants do not conduct. In mice, the D47A (No2) and G22R (Lop10) alleles are loss-of-function mutants, and D47A acts without strong dominant inhibition in oocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of a mouse Cx50 mutation associated with the No2 mouse cataract.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that the D47A mutation acts as a loss-of-function mutation without strong dominant inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: A novel GJA8 mutation is associated with autosomal dominant lamellar pulverulent cataract: further evidence for gap junction dysfunction in human cataract.
evidence.snippet: hCx50P88Q did not induce intercellular conductance and significantly inhibited gap junctional activity of co-expressed wild type hCx50 RNA in paired Xenopus oocytes.

nodes.description: Light-scattering opacity of the lens, present at birth or in early childhood, usually bilateral, with a morphology that varies between families. Changes at the same codon give different morphologies (P88S pulverulent, P88Q lamellar pulverulent or Y-sutural), so modifying factors also contribute.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in GJA8 (p.P88Q) is associated with "balloon-like" cataract with Y-sutural opacities in a family of Indian origin.
evidence.snippet: Mutations of the same codon have previously been described in British families with pulverulent cataract, suggesting that modifying factors may determine the type of cataract.

nodes.description: Small corneal diameter accompanying the cataract in many dominant families (V44E, R198Q, R198W, W45S, P189L).

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in GJA8 associated with autosomal dominant congenital cataract and microcornea.
evidence.snippet: This is the first report of mutations in GJA8 to be associated with autosomal dominant cataract and microcornea.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in GJA8 associated with jellyfish-like cataract in a family of Indian origin.
evidence.snippet: Affected individuals had a jellyfish-like cataract in association with microcornea.

nodes.description: Small eye with the cataract, reported for several missense alleles and most severe with D51N.

evidence.reference_title: New GJA8 variants and phenotypes highlight its critical role in a broad spectrum of eye anomalies.
evidence.snippet: Five of these co-segregated with cataracts and microphthalmia, whereas the variant p.(Gly94Arg) was identified in an individual with congenital aphakia, sclerocornea, microphthalmia and coloboma.

nodes.description: Mutant Cx50 subunits (P88S, P88Q, S50P, G22R, the c.670insA frameshift) accumulate in cytoplasmic membranes or the endoplasmic reticulum instead of forming gap junction plaques. The frameshift mutant also partially blocks transport of wild-type Cx50 to the plasma membrane. In mouse lenses carrying S50P or G22R, retained protein is accompanied by a modest unfolded protein response.
nodes.id: Mutant Connexin 50 Mistrafficking and Intracellular Retention

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function and impaired degradation of a cataract-associated mutant connexin50.
evidence.snippet: Taken together, these results suggest that the P to S mutation at amino acid residue 88 causes a defect that leads to decreased degradation and subsequent accumulation of hCx50P88S in a cellular structure different from aggresomes.

evidence.reference_title: A cataract-causing connexin 50 mutant is mislocalized to the ER due to loss of the fourth transmembrane domain and cytoplasmic domain.
evidence.snippet: Overexpression of the frameshift mutant partially inhibited the transport of wild type connexin 50 to the plasma membrane.

evidence.reference_title: The unfolded protein response is activated in connexin 50 mutant mouse lenses.
evidence.snippet: Mice homozygous for the S50P or G22R mutation of connexin 50 have reduced amounts of connexin 50 protein at the cell membrane, with some intracellular staining consistent with retention in the endoplasmic reticulum.

nodes.description: Opacity of the embryonal and fetal nucleus, often pulverulent.

evidence.reference_title: Connexin 50 mutation in a family with congenital "zonular nuclear" pulverulent cataract of Pakistani origin.
evidence.snippet: Here we describe a second mutation (E48K) in connexin 50 that confirms the involvement of this gene in cataractogenesis.

nodes.description: Second transmembrane domain; zonular pulverulent cataract in the original CZP1 family. Forms no channels, is a dominant negative inhibitor of wild-type Cx50, and accumulates intracellularly.

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in the human connexin50 gene (GJA8) underlies autosomal dominant "zonular pulverulent" cataract, on chromosome 1q.
evidence.snippet: This missense mutation is predicted to result in the nonconservative substitution of serine for a phylogenetically conserved proline (P88S).

nodes.description: Dust-like ("pulverulent") opacities, the morphology of the original CZP1 family.

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in the human connexin50 gene (GJA8) underlies autosomal dominant "zonular pulverulent" cataract, on chromosome 1q.
evidence.snippet: CZP1, a locus for autosomal dominant "zonular pulverulent" cataract, previously had been linked with the Duffy blood-group-antigen locus on chromosome 1q.

nodes.description: Lens fiber cells depend on Cx50 and Cx46 gap junctions to exchange ions, water and metabolites with the surface of the avascular lens. In Cx50 D47A mouse lenses, Cx50 and Cx46 protein levels fall and coupling between fibers drops, most in mature central fibers.
nodes.id: Reduced Lens Fiber Gap Junctional Coupling

animal_models.description: Heterozygous and homozygous lenses have reduced Cx50 and Cx46 levels and reduced fiber coupling.
animal_models.name: Gja8 D47A (No2) mouse

evidence.reference_title: The Connexin50D47A Mutant Causes Cataracts by Calcium Precipitation.
evidence.snippet: Gap junctional coupling in differentiating fibers of Cx50D47A lenses was 49% (heterozygotes) and 29% (homozygotes), and in mature fibers, it was 24% (heterozygotes) and 4% (homozygotes) compared to wild-type lenses.

nodes.description: Cx50-null mouse lenses and eyes are normal at birth but small by the end of the first postnatal week. In humans, some GJA8 alleles give microcornea or microphthalmia with the cataract.

animal_models.description: Null mice have microphthalmia, small lenses and zonular pulverulent nuclear cataracts.
animal_models.name: Gja8 knockout mouse

animal_models.description: Heterozygotes have pulverulent cataract with smaller eyes; homozygotes have marked microphthalmia with a hypoplastic lens.
animal_models.name: Gja8 L7Q (Dca) rat

evidence.reference_title: Targeted ablation of connexin50 in mice results in microphthalmia and zonular pulverulent cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Cx50-knockout eyes weighed 32% less than controls, whereas lens mass was reduced by 46%.

evidence.reference_title: New GJA8 variants and phenotypes highlight its critical role in a broad spectrum of eye anomalies.
evidence.snippet: In mice, missense mutations and homozygous Gja8 deletions lead to smaller lenses and microphthalmia in addition to cataract, suggesting that Gja8 may play a role in both lens development and ocular growth.

nodes.description: "Balloon-like" cataract with prominent Y-sutural opacities in one P88Q family.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in GJA8 (p.P88Q) is associated with "balloon-like" cataract with Y-sutural opacities in a family of Indian origin.
evidence.snippet: Affected individuals had "balloon-like" cataract with prominent Y-sutural opacities.

nodes.description: Dense triangular nuclear cataract in homozygotes for the recessive ins776G allele.

evidence.reference_title: A novel GJA8 mutation causing a recessive triangular cataract.
evidence.snippet: The proband, AD, has a dense, triangular nuclear cataract.

nodes.description: Opacity confined to a zone of the lens.

evidence.reference_title: A missense mutation in the human connexin50 gene (GJA8) underlies autosomal dominant "zonular pulverulent" cataract, on chromosome 1q.
evidence.snippet: Here we report genetic refinement of the CZP1 locus and show that the underlying mutation is present in GJA8, the gene for connexin50.

nodes.description: Recessive frameshift that replaces the C-terminal region; the mutant is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.

evidence.reference_title: A cataract-causing connexin 50 mutant is mislocalized to the ER due to loss of the fourth transmembrane domain and cytoplasmic domain.
evidence.snippet: Our results show that a frameshift mutant of connexin 50 mislocalizes to the ER and causes disintegration of the ERGIC and Golgi.
